name: Terbium
occurrence: Found in low concentrations in monazite and xenotime ores.
majorUses: Green phosphors in energy-efficient lighting and displays
notableCharacteristics: One of the four elements named after the single Swedish village of Ytterby (alongside yttrium, ytterbium, and erbium).
whyHere: Its nine 4f electrons give terbium ions a distinctive green light emission when excited, the exact property exploited in energy-efficient green phosphor coatings.
didYouKnow: Terbium is a key ingredient in Terfenol-D, an alloy that changes shape measurably in a magnetic field — a property called magnetostriction that's used in precision sonar transducers.
genZNote: One of four elements from the same tiny Swedish village. Also makes alloys that change shape in magnetic fields, which is objectively cool.
